prompt: Produce exactly one concise natural‑language caption (a single grammatical sentence) that vividly and precisely describes the main subject(s), visible actions, interactions and the setting; remain concrete, image‑centered and avoid speculation or subjective judgement. For every visible person or object state whether it is stationary or moving; when describing motion give horizontal direction first then vertical relative to the image frame (for example, "from left to right," "toward the camera while descending"), name any visible phase of motion (starting/ascending/peaking/descending/landing), and indicate whether motions are simultaneous or sequential. For each moving subject describe trajectory both relative to the main subject (passing to her right, approaching from behind, moving alongside) and relative to the camera (toward/away from the camera, to the left/right edge of the frame). Specify posture precisely (for example, "seated upright," "leaning forward," "weight shifted onto left leg," "knees bent") and the subject’s orientation to the camera (facing the camera, in profile, back to the camera). For every visible person report head orientation and precise gaze direction using clear phrases (for example, "looking directly at the camera," "eyes down at the phone," "gaze up and to the left," "looking toward the car"); if multiple people gaze at the same target state that relationship. When people interact, report only observable interaction cues and roles—describe who is addressing or reacting to whom using visible evidence (open mouth facing another as an indicator of speaking; turned body, raised hand or pointing as gestures; facing and still with closed mouth as listening or observing) and specify the nature and direction of gestures. For interactions with objects or structures state exactly how a subject is using them (holding, gripping, resting, pulling, supporting, leaning on), which hand and side (left/right), and whether the hand is in contact, gripping, merely near, or in motion versus resting; for static structures note orientation or alignment relative to nearby elements (for example, "platform oriented parallel to the riverbank"). Clarify precise spatial relationships, counts, arrangement, proximity and scale using camera‑relative language and clear phrases (foreground/midground/background; left/middle/right of frame; directly in front of/behind; clustered closely; a few feet/meters apart). Describe lighting, shadows and visible surface textures with observable cues and an approximate shadow direction or length when apparent (for example, "sunlit with long shadows toward the lower left," "diffuse overcast, little shadow"; "wet pavement reflecting light"); note absence of distinct shadows when visible. Report facial expressions or visible affect only when clearly evident using observable detail (for example, "open‑mouthed," "smiling with teeth visible," "furrowed brow"). Keep the sentence concise, factual and image‑specific; output exactly one single sentence as the caption.
